title: B.V.Sc. & A.H. versus B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture: regulatory, duration and admission differences
description: Compare the 5.5-year VCI-regulated B.V.Sc. & A.H. veterinary degree with the 4-year ICAR-aligned B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture programme.
summary: Applicants interested in animal health and crop sciences should compare two distinct professional frameworks: the 5.5-year B.V.Sc. & A.H. degree regulated by the Veterinary Council of India (VCI) and the 4-year B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture degree aligned with ICAR norms.

sections.heading: VCI clinical licensing versus ICAR agricultural education
paragraphs: A Bachelor of Veterinary Science and Animal Husbandry (B.V.Sc. & A.H.)—such as the programme profiled at [Khalsa College of Veterinary and Animal Sciences](/university/khalsa-college-of-veterinary-and-animal-sciences) under GADVASU, Ludhiana—spans five and a half years, including a compulsory one-year rotational clinical and livestock internship, and is governed by the Veterinary Council of India (VCI) minimum standards.

By contrast, [B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture](/bsc-agriculture) at institutions like [Khalsa College, Amritsar](/university/khalsa-college-amritsar) or [Guru Kashi University](/university/guru-kashi-university) is a four-year (eight-semester) degree focused on agronomy, soil science, genetics, plant protection, agricultural economics and final-year RAWE/ELP field modules.

sections.heading: Comparing NEET-UG/university veterinary counselling with agriculture entry routes
paragraphs: Veterinary admissions typically require Physics, Chemistry, Biology and English in Class 12 alongside NEET-UG or state veterinary university counselling (such as GADVASU), and carry distinct clinical and management-quota fee structures. Read [plan an agriculture study pathway after Class 12](/blogs/agriculture-study-plan-after-class-12) and [how to compare agriculture fees](/articles/agriculture-fee-budget).

faqs.question: Can a B.Sc. (Hons.) Agriculture graduate practice as a licensed veterinarian?
faqs.answer: No. Veterinary clinical practice and registration with a State Veterinary Council require a recognised B.V.Sc. & A.H. qualification under the Indian Veterinary Council Act.

faqs.question: Why is B.V.Sc. & A.H. 5.5 years long while B.Sc. Agriculture is 4 years?
faqs.answer: Under VCI regulations, B.V.Sc. & A.H. comprises 4.5專業 academic years plus a mandatory 12-month rotational clinical internship.
